# 2 Samuel Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 175v–176r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_008_page_001.jpg, 2SA_008_page_002.jpg

---

**1** After this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control, taking their chief city from their hands.

**2** He also defeated Moab. He made the prisoners lie on the ground and measured them off with a cord: two lengths to be executed, one length to be spared. The Moabites became David's subjects and paid tribute.

**3** David then defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as Hadadezer was on his way to reassert control along the Euphrates. **4** David captured seventeen hundred cavalrymen and twenty thousand infantry from him. He hamstrung all the chariot horses, keeping only enough for a hundred chariots.

**5** When the Arameans from Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David cut down twenty-two thousand of them. **6** He stationed garrisons throughout Aramean Damascus. The Arameans became David's subjects and paid tribute. The LORD gave David victory everywhere he went.

**7** David seized the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's officers and brought them to Jerusalem. **8** From Betah and Berothai, cities belonging to Hadadezer, King David carried off an enormous quantity of bronze.

**9** When King Toi of Hamath heard that David had crushed Hadadezer's entire army, **10** he sent his son Joram to congratulate David on his victory — since Hadadezer had been Toi's enemy too. Joram brought gifts of silver, gold, and bronze.

**11** King David consecrated all of it to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had taken from every nation he conquered — **12** Aram, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, Amalek, and the spoils from Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

**13** David's fame grew when he returned from crushing the Edomites in the Valley of Salt — eighteen thousand of them. **14** He put garrisons throughout Edom. All the Edomites became David's subjects. The LORD gave David victory everywhere he went.

**15** David ruled over all Israel. He governed his people with justice and fairness.

**16** Joab son of Zeruiah commanded the army. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the royal historian. **17** Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests. Seraiah was the royal secretary. **18** Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethite and Pelethite guards. And David's own sons served as royal officials.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — "their chief city":** The Hebrew *meteg ha-ammah* is deeply obscure — literally "the bridle of the cubit/forearm." I render the probable meaning: David took control of the Philistines' primary power center. The Chronicles parallel (1 Chr 18:1) confirms this refers to Gath.

**Verse 2 — "measured them off with a cord":** This is one of the most chilling passages in David's story. Prisoners of war are made to lie on the ground and are divided by measuring cord: two-thirds die, one-third live. The narrator records this with terrifying matter-of-factness.

**Verse 15 — "justice and fairness":** The Hebrew pair *mishpat u-tsedaqah* — justice and righteousness — is the signature vocabulary of ideal kingship in the Hebrew Bible. This verse is the narrative high point of David's reign: he is doing what a king is supposed to do.

**Verse 18 — "royal officials":** The Hebrew says David's sons were *kohanim* — priests. But since David's sons are not from the tribe of Levi, this likely means "chief officials" or "royal advisors" in a secular sense. The Chronicler rewrites this as "chief officials" (*rishonim*). I render "royal officials" to capture the probable meaning.

*— PNEUMA*
